newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CROFT AND GOUGH HALT AUSTRALIAN REVIVAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CROFT AND GOUGH HALT AUSTRALIAN REVIVAL.

text.p: The fluctuating first test edged back towards England as they captured three Australian wickets during the fourth afternoon at Edgbaston on Sunday.
Rain brought an early tea with the tourists 403 for five, only 43 runs ahead, with Steve Waugh 28 not out and Ian Healy not off the mark.
Australian prospects of achieving at least a draw after their miserable first two days were brighter at lunch, after Greg Blewett had made 125 to emulate captain Mark Taylor's 129.

After giving a return catch to Robert Croft, the captain departed to a standing ovation from all round the ground, having made his highest test score for three years to end any debate about his leadership.

Croft secured his third wicket of the innings when Blewett was given out to a catch at silly point by Mark Butcher, the ball possibly touching his glove after bouncing off a pad. Blewett had become the only player to make a hundred in each of his first three Ashes tests.

The partnership of 194 was easily the best for Australia in an Edgbaston test, beating the record held by Mark and Steve Waugh in 1993. And Blewett made history by becoming the only player to make a century in each of his first three England-Australia matches.
Steve Waugh was fortunate to survive when a ball from Devon Malcolm bounced off his bat and foot onto the stumps without dislodging a bail.

But with the home crowd growing more vociferous in their support again, Darren Gough returned to the attack to expose Michael Bevan's weakness against short-pitched bowling. Bevan gave Nasser Hussain an easy catch in the gully, having scored 24, and Mark Waugh lasted only seven balls before touching Gough to wicketkeeper Alex Stewart for one.
Waugh had been discharged from hospital after an overnight stay, diagnosed as suffering only from a virus, not appendicitis as had been feared.
